hook: A wave flipped his boat just as the rescue swimmer moved in.
narration: A breaking wave flipped this boat just as the rescue swimmer moved in.
Twenty foot seas, at the mouth of the Columbia River, in Oregon.
The Jayhawk crew had come from across the country for advanced rescue school.
The wind was extreme, and the seas kept breaking.
The swimmer reached the mariner in the water.
A swimmer and a survivor ride the same winch cable up, clipped together.
It was the swimmer's first life saved.
outcome: The mariner came through in stable condition.
title: Wave flipped his boat in 20 foot seas
description:
A breaking wave capsized a vessel in 20-foot seas near the mouth of the Columbia River, Oregon, in February 2023. A Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk crew from Aviation Training Center Mobile, in Oregon for the Advanced Rescue Helicopter School, hoisted the mariner from the water.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video (USCG Heartland), via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ATC_Mobile_MH-60_aircrew_rescues_a_mariner_at_the_mouth_of_the_Columbia_River_near_Astoria.webm

question_comment: Would you cross the Columbia River bar in 20 foot seas?

extra_sources.excerpt: On scene conditions were reported to be 20-foot seas and extremely high windspeeds.
As the swimmer made his approach, a breaking wave capsized the vessel.
The swimmer proceeded to retrieve the mariner from the water and both were hoisted to the helicopter using a winch cable.
As a rescue swimmer, this was Aviation Survival Technician 3rd Class John 'Branch' Walton's first life saved. Hours later, he and his classmates graduated from the Advanced Rescue Helicopter School.
was in stable condition when transferred from the Coast Guard's care.
